The Dhān-Sya Thit states that in Nānatthakosa, the word Amata in neuter gender is in the sense of remnant of sacrifice, ambrosia, water, butter, wealth got with asking for and Nibbāna. In masculine gender, it is in the senses of deity, Dhanvantarī medic. In the feminine gender, it is in the senses of cardamon, long pepper, myrobalam, moonseed vine, gooseberry. It states in its footnote of Dhān-ṭī,25 that the same meanings. Moreover, in Kotthubha, it is in the senses of (Abyayībhāva) 1. deathless, (2) immortal, (3) free from perishing, everlasting; he; thing. (Masc.) (1) deva. (6) one who kills the poisonous tree. (7) remnant of sacrifice. (8) food obtained without asking. (9) water. (10) alcohol made by cooking and distilling sugar and brown slab-sugar together, sweet alcohol. (11) butter. (12) cow-milk. (13) edible food. (14) rice. (15) sentient being, thing which is adorable, desirable. (16) gold. (17) mercury. (18) poison. (19) Brahmā, in Vācappati, 40 meanings are mentioned.] (Neut.)
